title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
notes: Chemical Reaction: A process in which new chemicals are formed.
Chemical Equation: A chemical reaction written with symbols and formulas.
In an equation, reactants are written on the left-hand side (LHS) and products on the right-hand side (RHS): Reactant -> Product.
State symbols used in equations: (aq) = soluble in water, (ppt) = insoluble in water, (s) = solid, (g) = gas, (l) = liquid.
Balanced Chemical Equation: The number of atoms of each element must be the same on the LHS and RHS, since mass is conserved (total mass of reactants = total mass of products).
Balancing trick: First balance metals (Zn, Fe, Na, Al, Mg, Mn, Cu, Ca, Pb, Ba), second balance non-metals (Cl, Br, S, N, C), and third balance oxygen, then hydrogen.

Combination Reaction: Two or more reactants combine to form a single product. Example: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO (burning of magnesium ribbon gives dazzling white light and white powder; this is an exothermic reaction).
Example of combination and exothermic reaction: CaO (quicklime) + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime). Quicklime reacts vigorously with water and there is a rise in temperature.
Example: C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g) (burning of coal).

Decomposition Reaction: One reactant breaks down into two or more products. Types: (1) Thermal decomposition - breaks due to heat, (2) Electrolytic decomposition - breaks due to electric current, (3) Photochemical decomposition - breaks due to light (photolysis).
Thermal decomposition examples: CaCO3 (limestone) --heat--> CaO (quicklime) + CO2; 2FeSO4 (green) --heat--> Fe2O3 (red/brown) + SO2 + SO3; 2Pb(NO3)2 (white) --heat--> 2PbO (yellow/brown) + 4NO2 + O2.
All three thermal decomposition examples above are endothermic reactions. SO2 and SO3 gases produced are air pollutants.

Electrolytic decomposition example: 2H2O(l) --electrolysis--> 2H2(g) + O2(g). Volume ratio H2:O2 = 2:1. Pure water is a poor conductor of electricity, so a few drops of acid are added which act as an electrolyte and conduct electricity.

Photochemical decomposition (photolysis) examples: 2AgCl (white) --sunlight--> 2Ag (grey) + Cl2(g); 2AgBr (yellow) --sunlight--> 2Ag (grey) + Br2(g). This principle is used in black and white photography.
Displacement Reaction: A more reactive element replaces a less reactive element from its salt solution. A + BC -> AC + B (A displaces B).

Reactivity Series (most reactive to least reactive): Potassium (K) > Sodium (Na) > Calcium (Ca) > Magnesium (Mg) > Aluminium (Al) > Zinc (Zn) > Iron (Fe) > Lead (Pb) > Hydrogen (H) > Copper (Cu) > Mercury (Hg) > Silver (Ag) > Gold (Au).
Displacement example: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq, blue) -> FeSO4(aq, green) + Cu(s, red/brown).
Displacement example: Zn(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> ZnSO4 + Cu.

Displacement example: Zn(s) + H2SO4(aq) -> ZnSO4 + H2 + Heat. H2 gas is colourless and odourless, burns with a pop sound and extinguishes a burning candle. Temperature increases, so the reaction is exothermic.
Double Displacement Reaction: Exchange of ions between reactants. A+B- + C+D- -> AD + CB.
Double displacement example: Na2SO4(aq, colourless) + BaCl2(aq, colourless) -> BaSO4(s, white precipitate) + 2NaCl.
Double displacement example: Pb(NO3)2 (colourless) + 2KI (colourless) -> PbI2 (yellow precipitate) + 2KNO3. This is an example of a double displacement and precipitation reaction.

Heat in reactions - Exothermic Reaction: A -> C + Heat. Examples: (1) Respiration: Glucose + O2 -> CO2(g) + H2O(l) + Energy. (2) Burning of natural gas: CH4(g) + O2(g) -> CO2(g) + H2O(g) + Heat. (3) Decomposition of vegetables into compost.
Heat in reactions - Endothermic Reaction: A --heat--> C. Mostly decomposition reactions are endothermic. Examples: 2FeSO4 --heat--> Fe2O3(s) + SO2(g) + SO3(g); CaCO3(s) --heat--> CaO + CO2(g).
Redox Reaction: The reaction in which oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
Oxidation: If a chemical (A) undergoes loss of electron / gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen, it is called oxidation of A, and A is said to be oxidised. Example: Cu(s) + O2(g) --heat--> CuO(s).
Reduction: If a chemical (B) undergoes gain of electron / loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen, it is called reduction of B, and B is said to be reduced. Example: CuO(s) + H2(g) --heat--> Cu(s) + H2O.
Oxidising agent - causes oxidation, gets reduced itself. Reducing agent - causes reduction, gets oxidised itself.
Redox example: ZnO + C -> Zn + CO. Here ZnO is the oxidising agent (gets reduced), C is the reducing agent (gets oxidised).

Corrosion: When a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture (water vapour + oxygen), acid, etc., it is said to corrode; this process is called corrosion. Examples: (1) Rusting of iron - hydrated reddish brown iron oxide (rust). (2) Tarnishing of copper - green. (3) Tarnishing of silver - black.

Rancidity: The taste or smell of food material containing fat/oil changes when it is left exposed to air for a long time. Oxidation of fat/oil present in food material causes rancidity. Prevention: adding antioxidants, storing food in air-tight containers, flushing with N2 gas.

Physical Change: No chemical reaction happens, no new chemical is formed, only shape/size/state changes. Examples: boiling water, evaporating dish, melting of ice to give water, melting of wax, crushing a paper cup, crystallisation.

Chemical Change: A chemical reaction happens, a new substance is formed, both physical and chemical properties change. Examples: burning of paper, fermentation of grapes, souring of milk, curd from milk, rusting of iron, food digestion, food cooking, chemical battery usage.

examples.question: What happens when zinc granules are added to dilute sulphuric acid?
examples.solution: Zn(s) + H2SO4(aq) -> ZnSO4(aq) + H2(g) + Heat. Colourless, odourless hydrogen gas is evolved which burns with a pop sound; the reaction is exothermic.

examples.question: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction?
examples.solution: Glucose + O2 -> CO2 + H2O + Energy. Energy is released during the breakdown of glucose, so it is exothermic.

examples.question: Identify the oxidising and reducing agent in ZnO + C -> Zn + CO.
examples.solution: ZnO loses oxygen and is reduced, so it is the oxidising agent. C gains oxygen and is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent.
